sentences.text: The known skeleton of Gongxianosaurus is largely complete but lacks the hands and most of the skull.
This animal may have reached a length of 14 meters.
Fossils were discovered in May 1997 during a geological exploration.
The holotype specimen was likely destroyed when the protective exhibition hall built over it collapsed.
Excavation of the site recovered a wealth of fossils from an area of approximately 200 square meters.

Unlike other sauropods, it lacked pleurocoels, suggesting its vertebrae were quite massive.
The pedal phalangeal formula of the foot is 2-3-4-5-1.
All digits except the outermost one ended in claws.
The chevrons of the tail were unbifurcated.
The genus Gongxianosaurus was established by He et al. in 1998.
The species Gongxianosaurus shibeiensis was established by He et al. in 1998.
Gongxianosaurus belongs to the parent group Sauropodiformes.
It is classified within the dinosaur class Saurischia.
The type species of the genus is Gongxianosaurus shibeiensis.
Cladistic analyses of Gongxianosaurus are limited because its fossils have not yet been fully described.
Gongxianosaurus lived during the early Jurassic Period, specifically the Sinemurian to Pliensbachian stages.
It lived approximately 183 to 174 million years ago during the Toarcian age.
Gongxianosaurus lived in what is now Asia.
It lived during the Toarcian stage, between 184.2 and 174.7 million years ago.
It is debated whether some fossils belong to Gongxianosaurus shibeiensis or a second species, with Ouyang Hui informally naming the latter Yibinosaurus zhoui.
